scenario_text: A 45-year-old female presents to the emergency department with the sudden onset of the worst headache of her life ('thunderclap' headache). No focal neurological deficits. Vital signs are normal. Suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage.
notes: Emergent CT head to rule out SAH is standard first line.

scenario_text: A 28-year-old male presents with acute onset of severe pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and tachycardia. D-dimer is elevated. Low risk for PE but clinical concern remains high.
notes: CTA is the standard gold standard for suspected pulmonary embolism.

scenario_text: A 67-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation presents with acute onset of severe, diffuse abdominal pain out of proportion to physical exam findings. High concern for acute mesenteric ischemia.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: Mesenteric ischemia evaluation requires IV contrast.

scenario_text: A 52-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to his back, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Amylase and lipase are significantly elevated. Suspected acute pancreatitis.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: IV contrast is useful to assess for pancreatic necrosis.

scenario_text: A 35-year-old female presents with acute pain, swelling, and tenderness in the right lower extremity after a long flight. High pretest probability for deep vein thrombosis.
notes: Duplex ultrasound is the diagnostic method of choice for DVT.

scenario_text: A 22-year-old female presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain for 12 hours, low-grade fever, and leukocytosis. She is not pregnant. Suspected acute appendicitis.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: CT with contrast is highly sensitive and specific for appendicitis in adult non-pregnant patients.

scenario_text: A 72-year-old male presents with acute onset of left-sided hemiparesis and facial droop that started 2 hours ago. National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score is 14. Suspected acute ischemic stroke.
notes: Non-contrast CT head is the critical first step to exclude hemorrhage prior to thrombolysis.

scenario_text: A 55-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presents with progressive back pain that is worse at night and when lying down. Suspected spinal cord compression.
expected_modality: MRI spine lumbar without and with contrast
notes: MRI is the most sensitive modality for suspected spinal metastasis and cord compression.

scenario_text: A 30-year-old male presents with severe right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria, and nausea. Suspected renal colic.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
notes: Non-contrast CT (low dose stone protocol) is the preferred imaging modality for suspected urolithiasis.

scenario_text: A 4-year-old female presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting. Suspected acute appendicitis.
notes: Ultrasound is the preferred initial imaging modality in pediatric patients to avoid radiation.

scenario_text: A 14-month-old male is brought to the emergency department after falling from a changing table (approx. 3 feet) onto a hardwood floor. He has a 2-cm hematoma over the temporal skull. He is awake but irritable. Suspected pediatric head trauma.
notes: CT is appropriate for clinically significant traumatic brain injury risk based on PECARN criteria.

scenario_text: A 60-year-old male with a 40 pack-year smoking history presents with a new cough, hemoptysis, and 15 lb weight loss over 2 months. Chest X-ray shows a suspicious right hilar mass.
notes: CT chest with contrast is the initial staging modality of choice for suspected lung cancer.

scenario_text: A 48-year-old female presents with a palpable painless lump in her upper outer quadrant of the left breast. She has no family history of breast cancer.
notes: Diagnostic mammography is the initial evaluation for a palpable breast mass in women 30 years and older.

scenario_text: A 29-year-old female, G2P1 at 24 weeks gestation, presents with acute onset of right lower quadrant pain, nausea, and leukocytosis. Suspected acute appendicitis in pregnancy.
notes: Ultrasound is the initial imaging modality of choice for suspected appendicitis in pregnant patients.

scenario_text: A 62-year-old male presents with sudden onset of severe, tearing chest pain radiating to the back. Blood pressure is 180/100 mmHg. Suspected acute aortic dissection.
expected_modality: CTA chest and abdomen with contrast
notes: CTA is highly accurate for defining the presence and extent of aortic dissection.

scenario_text: A 50-year-old female presents with persistent left hip pain for 6 months, worse with weight-bearing. Plain radiographs of the hip are normal. Suspected early avascular necrosis.
notes: MRI is the most sensitive modality for diagnosing early osteonecrosis when radiographs are negative.

scenario_text: A 19-year-old male sustained a non-contact pivoting injury to his right knee during a basketball game. He felt a 'pop' followed by immediate swelling. Normal plain radiographs. Suspected ACL tear.
notes: MRI is the modality of choice for evaluating internal joint derangement of the knee.

scenario_text: A 38-year-old female presents with chronic generalized musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and multiple tender points. No joint swelling. Normal inflammatory markers. Suspected fibromyalgia.
notes: Imaging is generally not indicated for fibromyalgia unless looking for alternative diagnoses.

scenario_text: A 68-year-old male presents with persistent low back pain for 2 months. No red flags (no fever, no history of cancer, no weight loss, no focal neurological deficit). Radiographs show mild degenerative changes.
notes: Routine imaging is not recommended for uncomplicated low back pain without red flags.

scenario_text: A 75-year-old female with osteoporosis presents with sudden onset of severe thoracic back pain after a minor slip. Radiographs show a compression fracture of T12 of indeterminate age. High clinical suspicion for acute fracture.
notes: MRI is useful to determine the age of a compression fracture and presence of edema.

scenario_text: A 45-year-old male presents with persistent pain in the right shoulder, worse with overhead activity and night pain. Active range of motion is limited. Plain radiographs are normal. Suspected rotator cuff tear.
notes: MRI is highly accurate for detecting rotator cuff tears.

scenario_text: A 30-year-old female presents with acute onset of right ankle pain and inability to bear weight after a twisting injury. Bony tenderness at the posterior edge of the lateral malleolus.
notes: Radiographs are indicated based on Ottawa Ankle Rules.

scenario_text: A 58-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis presents with new onset of ascites and encephalopathy. Diagnostic ultrasound of the liver is required.
notes: Ultrasound is the screening and diagnostic modality of choice for liver parenchymal changes and ascites.

scenario_text: A 63-year-old female presents with painless gross hematuria. Urinalysis shows numerous RBCs per high-power field. No history of trauma. Suspected urinary tract malignancy.
expected_modality: CT urography with and without contrast
notes: CT urography is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating painless hematuria in adults.

scenario_text: A 35-year-old female presents with chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and deep dyspareunia. Suspected endometriosis.
notes: Transvaginal ultrasound is the initial imaging modality of choice for pelvic pain in females.

scenario_text: A 52-year-old male presents with a new onset of generalized tonic-clonic seizure. No history of epilepsy. Normal vital signs, no trauma.
expected_modality: MRI brain without and with contrast
notes: MRI is the preferred imaging study for evaluating new-onset seizures in adults.

scenario_text: A 70-year-old female presents with sudden onset of fleeting vision loss in the left eye ('amaurosis fugax') lasting 5 minutes. No other neurological symptoms. Suspected carotid artery disease.
notes: Carotid duplex ultrasound is the initial test of choice for suspected carotid stenosis.

scenario_text: A 42-year-old male presents with chronic cough and mild dyspnea for 3 months. Normal physical exam. Suspected interstitial lung disease.
notes: High-resolution chest CT without contrast is the gold standard for diagnosing ILD.

scenario_text: A 31-year-old female presents with 1 week of progressive numbness and tingling in both legs, along with mild urinary urgency. History of optic neuritis 2 years ago. Suspected multiple sclerosis relapse.
expected_modality: MRI brain and spine without and with contrast
notes: MRI of brain and spine is the standard for detecting active demyelinating lesions.

scenario_text: A 50-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of vertigo, tinnitus, and sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear. Suspected acoustic neuroma.
expected_modality: MRI internal auditory canals without and with contrast
notes: Contrast-enhanced MRI of the IACs is the study of choice for vestibular schwannoma.

scenario_text: A 25-year-old female presents with left calf pain and swelling. Low risk for DVT, Wells score of 0. D-dimer is normal.
notes: No imaging is indicated for low-probability DVT patients with a normal D-dimer.

scenario_text: A 60-year-old female with a history of renal cell carcinoma presents for routine surveillance 2 years after partial nephrectomy.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: Contrast-enhanced CT is the standard for post-operative surveillance of RCC.

scenario_text: A 3-year-old male is brought in by his mother due to a limp in the right leg. He has a low-grade fever and refuses to bear weight on the right hip. Inflammatory markers are elevated. Suspected transient synovitis or septic arthritis.
notes: Hip ultrasound is the test of choice to detect hip effusion in a child with a limp.

scenario_text: A 45-year-old male presents with severe right upper quadrant pain, fever, and a positive Murphy's sign on physical exam. Suspected acute cholecystitis.
notes: Ultrasound is the most sensitive and specific test for diagnosing acute cholecystitis.

scenario_text: A 74-year-old female presents with acute onset of severe, diffuse abdominal pain, abdominal distention, and high-pitched bowel sounds. Radiographs show dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels. Suspected small bowel obstruction.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: CT with contrast is indicated to determine the site and cause of obstruction, and assess for ischemia.

scenario_text: A 28-year-old female presents with persistent pelvic pain and a palpable right adnexal mass on pelvic exam. She is not pregnant.
notes: Transvaginal ultrasound is the primary modality to characterize adnexal masses.

scenario_text: A 50-year-old female presents with left lower quadrant abdominal pain for 2 days, low-grade fever, and mild leukocytosis. No signs of peritonitis. Suspected acute diverticulitis.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: CT with contrast is the gold standard for diagnosing and staging diverticulitis.

scenario_text: A 67-year-old male presents with chronic, progressive dyspnea and cough. He was exposed to asbestos for 30 years as a shipyard worker. Suspected asbestosis or pleural plaques.
notes: Non-contrast CT chest (or HRCT) is indicated for asbestos-related pleural and parenchymal disease.

scenario_text: A 34-year-old male presents with acute onset of sharp chest pain that is worse when lying flat and relieved by sitting forward. EKG shows diffuse ST-segment elevation. Suspected acute pericarditis.
notes: Echocardiography is the initial test of choice to evaluate for pericardial effusion.

scenario_text: A 72-year-old female presents with a palpable nodule in the left lobe of the thyroid. She has no history of radiation exposure. TSH is normal.
notes: Ultrasound is the primary modality for evaluating thyroid nodules.

scenario_text: A 21-year-old male presents with a high-velocity injury to his left wrist after falling onto an outstretched hand (FOOSH). Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Radiographs are normal. Suspected occult scaphoid fracture.
notes: MRI is highly sensitive for occult scaphoid fractures when initial radiographs are negative.

scenario_text: A 55-year-old male presents with acute onset of painful swelling in the left first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint. Joint aspirate shows negatively birefringent crystals. Suspected acute gouty arthritis.
notes: Routine imaging is not indicated for the diagnosis of acute gout when crystal-proven.

scenario_text: A 40-year-old female presents with chronic headache of 3 months duration. It is constant, bilateral, and tension-like. Normal neurological exam, no red flags.
notes: Imaging is not indicated for tension-type headaches without atypical features.

scenario_text: A 5-year-old female presents with persistent constipation and abdominal pain. No alarm symptoms. Normal growth and development.
notes: Routine abdominal radiographs are not recommended for functional constipation in children.

scenario_text: A 64-year-old female presents with severe pain and swelling in her right calf after a knee arthroscopy 1 week ago. Low-grade fever. Suspected postoperative DVT.
notes: Postoperative DVT evaluation requires duplex ultrasound.

scenario_text: A 70-year-old male presents with chronic, dull abdominal pain, weight loss, and painless jaundice. Courvoisier's sign is positive. Suspected pancreatic head mass.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: Multidetector CT with pancreatic protocol is the gold standard for staging pancreatic cancer.

scenario_text: A 38-year-old male presents with persistent low back pain radiating down the left leg to the foot (sciatica) for 8 weeks. Normal strength and reflexes. Has not tried conservative therapy.
notes: Imaging is generally not indicated for acute radiculopathy before a trial of conservative management.

scenario_text: A 12-year-old male presents with severe left testicular pain that started suddenly 3 hours ago. The left testis is swollen, tender, and high-riding. Left cremasteric reflex is absent. Suspected testicular torsion.
notes: Color Doppler ultrasound of the scrotum is the test of choice for suspected testicular torsion.

scenario_text: A 59-year-old female presents with transient ischemic attack (TIA) symptoms (right-hand weakness and slurred speech) that resolved completely within 30 minutes. Normal neurological exam.
expected_modality: MRI brain without and with contrast
notes: MRI with DWI is the gold standard for identifying ischemic injury in TIA patients.

scenario_text: A 49-year-old male presents with a new onset of dull right-sided chest pain. History of asbestos exposure. Chest radiograph shows pleural thickening. Suspected mesothelioma.
notes: CT chest with contrast is the initial staging modality of choice for suspected pleural mesothelioma.

scenario_text: A 68-year-old female presents with progressive dementia, gait disturbance, and urinary incontinence ('wet, wacky, and wobbly'). Suspected normal pressure hydrocephalus.
notes: MRI brain without contrast is indicated to evaluate for ventriculomegaly and exclude other causes.

scenario_text: A 24-year-old female athlete presents with localized pain in the right tibia that is worse with running and relieved by rest. Point tenderness over the anterior tibia. Radiographs are normal. Suspected stress fracture.
notes: MRI is the most sensitive imaging modality for early stress injuries of bone.

scenario_text: A 41-year-old male presents with chronic, purulent nasal discharge, facial pain, and nasal congestion for 14 weeks. Unresponsive to medical therapy. Suspected chronic rhinosinusitis.
notes: Non-contrast sinus CT is the standard modality to evaluate chronic rhinosinusitis before surgery.

scenario_text: A 63-year-old male with a history of heavy smoking presents with a pulsatile abdominal mass on routine physical exam. He has no abdominal pain. Suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm.
notes: Ultrasound is the screening and monitoring method of choice for AAA.

scenario_text: A 30-year-old female presents with acute pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, and a positive pregnancy test. G1P0 at 6 weeks gestation. Suspected ectopic pregnancy.
notes: Transvaginal ultrasound is the primary imaging modality for suspected ectopic pregnancy.

scenario_text: A 50-year-old male presents with macroscopic hematuria. Renal function is normal. Diagnostic workup for renal mass.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with and without contrast
notes: CT with and without contrast (renal mass protocol) is indicated to characterize renal tumors.

scenario_text: A 58-year-old female presents with severe pain in her left leg when walking 2 blocks, which is relieved by rest (claudication). Ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.6. Suspected peripheral arterial disease.
notes: CTA is highly accurate for planning revascularization in symptomatic PAD.

scenario_text: A 66-year-old female presents with acute, sharp right-sided chest pain and mild dyspnea. Vital signs are normal. Normal D-dimer. Low clinical risk for PE.
notes: PE imaging is not indicated in low-risk patients with a normal D-dimer.

scenario_text: A 45-year-old male presents with a persistent, non-healing ulcer on his left heel. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Bone is exposed. Suspected osteomyelitis.
notes: MRI is the most sensitive and specific modality for diagnosing diabetic foot osteomyelitis.

scenario_text: A 35-year-old female presents with a new onset of severe right-sided throbbing headache with nausea and photophobia. She has a history of similar self-limiting episodes. Normal physical exam. Suspected migraine.
notes: Routine imaging is not recommended for recurrent migraine headaches with normal exams.

scenario_text: A 51-year-old female with a history of colon cancer presents for routine surveillance 1 year after hemicolectomy.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: CT is standard for surveillance of colon cancer recurrence.

scenario_text: A 23-year-old male presents with right hip pain after a fall from a height. Radiographs show a suspicious radiolucent lesion in the femoral neck. Suspected benign vs. malignant bone tumor.
notes: CT is excellent for detailed characterization of bone architecture and mineral matrix.

scenario_text: A 65-year-old male presents with severe pain and swelling in his left knee. He is unable to bend the knee. Suspected septic arthritis. Joint fluid analysis shows high WBC count.
notes: Diagnostic imaging (other than radiographs) is not primary; joint aspiration is diagnostic.

scenario_text: A 4-year-old male is brought in by parents after swallowing a coin. He is drooling and refuses to eat. Suspected foreign body ingestion.
notes: Plain radiographs are indicated to locate radiopaque foreign bodies in the GI tract.

scenario_text: A 28-year-old female presents with chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Suspected Crohn's disease.
notes: MR enterography is the preferred modality for evaluating small bowel Crohn's disease.

scenario_text: A 73-year-old male presents with chronic, dull back pain. He has a history of prostate cancer and is on androgen deprivation therapy. Suspected bone metastases.
notes: Radionuclide bone scan is the standard initial screening tool for prostate cancer bone metastasis.

scenario_text: A 60-year-old female presents with acute, severe pain in her right upper quadrant. Ultrasound is inconclusive for cholecystitis. Suspected acute cholecystitis.
notes: Cholescintigraphy (HIDA scan) is the preferred second-line test for acute cholecystitis.

scenario_text: A 36-year-old male presents with sudden onset of excruciating pain in the left loin, radiating to the groin. Microscopic hematuria. Unwilling to undergo radiation. Suspected renal colic.
notes: Ultrasound is a reasonable alternative to CT for renal colic when radiation is contraindicated.

scenario_text: A 50-year-old female presents with new onset of left arm weakness. Brain MRI is contraindicated due to a non-MRI compatible pacemaker. Suspected acute ischemic stroke.
notes: CT head is the appropriate fallback for stroke imaging when MRI is contraindicated.

scenario_text: A 68-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease presents with atypical chest pain. Patient is at intermediate risk. Suspected coronary stenosis.
notes: Coronary CTA is appropriate for intermediate-risk patients with chest pain.

scenario_text: A 42-year-old female presents with chronic fatigue, weight gain, and dry skin. Normal physical exam. Suspected hypothyroidism.
notes: Imaging is not indicated for primary hypothyroidism unless a nodule is felt.

scenario_text: A 29-year-old male presents with persistent pain in the left wrist after a fall. Plain radiographs show a normal alignment and no fracture. Still tender in the anatomic snuffbox. Hand surgeon suspects occult fracture.
notes: CT is an acceptable alternative to MRI for diagnosing occult scaphoid fractures.

scenario_text: A 72-year-old female presents with sudden onset of dyspnea and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. D-dimer is high. CTA chest is contraindicated due to severe renal impairment (eGFR 15).
notes: V/Q scan is the preferred alternative for PE imaging when contrast CT is contraindicated.

scenario_text: A 55-year-old female presents with chronic pelvic pain and pressure. Ultrasound shows a large multi-septated cystic ovarian mass. Suspected ovarian cancer.
expected_modality: MRI pelvis without and with contrast
notes: MRI is indicated for further characterization of indeterminate adnexal masses.

scenario_text: A 32-year-old male presents with lower extremity swelling. He is asymptomatic otherwise. Normal physical exam. Low suspicion for DVT.
notes: No imaging is indicated for asymptomatic patients with low pretest probability.

scenario_text: A 60-year-old male presents with acute onset of severe, diffuse abdominal pain. Abdominal radiographs show free air under the diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum). Suspected perforated viscus.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
notes: CT with contrast is the gold standard to locate the site of perforation and evaluate severity.

scenario_text: A 40-year-old female presents with a new onset of chorea and psychiatric changes. Family history of Huntington's disease.
notes: MRI brain is indicated to assess for caudate atrophy and rule out other causes.

scenario_text: A 69-year-old female presents with a history of long-standing hypertension and sudden onset of double vision. Right CN VI palsy is noted on exam. Normal blood sugar.
expected_modality: MRI brain without and with contrast
notes: MRI is indicated for microvascular or neoplastic causes of cranial nerve palsies.

scenario_text: A 25-year-old male presents with persistent cough for 2 weeks after a cold. Normal vital signs, clear lungs on auscultation. No dyspnea, no fever. Suspected uncomplicated acute bronchitis.
notes: Imaging is not indicated for uncomplicated acute bronchitis in healthy adults.

scenario_text: A 48-year-old female presents with chronic, dull pain in the left flank. Urinalysis shows microscopic hematuria. Ultrasound shows a complex 3-cm cystic mass in the left kidney.
expected_modality: CT abdomen and pelvis with and without contrast
notes: Contrast-enhanced CT (renal protocol) is required to characterize complex renal cysts.
